template.apply.gone.note: Why Choose Connections skipped an agent: it was removed meanwhile.

template.apply.running.text: it runs, and that connection is another CLI's: stop it first
template.apply.running.note: Why Choose Connections skipped an agent: a connection of another CLI can't apply while it runs.

template.connections.ambiguous.text: connections: several are called "{ref}": name one by its id ({ids}).
template.connections.ambiguous.note: An answer in connections names several connections usable here. {ids} lists their ids.

template.connections.bad.text: connections: {keys} {count, plural, =1 {is} other {are}} not "*", a role ({roles}) or one of its agents: {agents}.
template.connections.bad.note: Keys in connections that are none of what it takes. {count} is how many, choosing the verb.

template.connections.both.text: connections: "{first}" and "{key}" both name agent {place} ({agent}): give it one connection.
template.connections.both.note: Two keys in connections name the same agent.

template.connections.none.note: No connection is usable here: the end of template.connections.required.

template.connections.notObject.text: connections is an object: "*", a role ({roles}), or an agent's place ("1") or name → a connection's id or name.
template.connections.notObject.note: A load's or Choose Connections' connections isn't an object (HI-2109). {roles} lists the roles.

template.connections.notText.text: connections.{key} is not a connection's id or name.
template.connections.notText.note: An answer in connections isn't text.

template.connections.range.text: connections: {key} is out of range: there are {count} agents ({agents}).
template.connections.range.note: A place in connections is beyond the agents. {count} is digits.

template.connections.required.text: connections is required: "*", a role ({roles}), or an agent's place ("1") or name → a connection's id or name. Its agents: {agents}. Usable here: {usable}.
template.connections.required.note: Choose Connections was given no answer. {usable} lists the connections it can use, or template.connections.none.

template.connections.several.text: connections: "{key}" is {count} of its agents: name each by its place ({choices}).
template.connections.several.note: A key in connections is several agents' name. {count} is digits.

template.connections.unknown.text: connections: no connection "{ref}" can be used here (options lists those that can).
template.connections.unknown.note: An answer in connections names no connection usable here.

template.find.from.note: A template call's from isn't text.

template.find.none.text: No template "{template}"{scoped, select, yes { in the {scope} scope} other {}}{fromProject, select, yes { kept in {from}} other {}}: list gives them.
template.find.none.note: No template has that file or name, in the scope or project named, if any.

template.find.required.text: template is required: its file or name, as list gives them

template.find.scope.text: scope is hive, workspace or project
template.find.scope.note: A template call's scope isn't one of the three. They are the argument's values.

template.find.several.text: Several templates are called "{template}": name one by scope and file ({choices}).
template.find.several.note: More than one template has that name: never one picked for the caller. {choices} lists each as "scope: file".

template.find.unusable.note: The template named can't be read or used. {problem} is why.

template.load.needsGit.text: Its workflow is for Git and this project has no version control: set up Git in the project's Version Control first (that is the user's choice), or load with workflow: false for its agents alone.
template.load.needsGit.note: Why a template's workflow can't be loaded (HI-1910): Hive never sets up Git for the Assistant.

template.load.notYet.text: The template can't be loaded yet: {blocked}
template.load.notYet.note: A load refused: {blocked} is each reason, joined by spaces.

template.load.optionsChanged.text: its options changed meanwhile, so they weren't saved: set them in the project's Version Control
template.load.optionsChanged.note: Why a loaded template's workflow wasn't saved: the project's options changed while it loaded.

template.load.tooMany.text: It has {count} agents, and this project's workflow allows {max} (Maximum agents, the user's team size, in Version Control → Workflow). The user can load it themselves, or raise Maximum agents first.
template.load.tooMany.note: Why the Assistant can't load a template (HI-2001): more agents than the project's Maximum agents, which only the Assistant's loads keep to. {count} and {max} are digits.

template.load.workflowCant.text: Its workflow can't be saved here: {problems}
template.load.workflowCant.note: A load refused: the template's workflow doesn't fit this project. {problems} is each reason.

template.names.both.text: names: "{first}" and "{key}" both name agent {place} ({agent}): give it one name.
template.names.both.note: Two keys in a load's names name the same agent.

template.names.none.text: names: no agent "{key}" in the template. Its agents: {keys}.
template.names.none.note: A key in a load's names names no agent.

template.names.notObject.text: names is an object: an agent's place or name → its new name. Its agents: {keys}.
template.names.notObject.note: A load's names isn't an object. {keys} lists its agents as "place (name)".

template.names.notText.text: names.{key} is not text: give each agent's new name as a string.
template.names.notText.note: A new name in a load's names isn't text.

template.names.range.text: names: {key} is out of range: the template has {count} agents ({keys}).
template.names.range.note: A place in a load's names is beyond the template's agents. {count} is digits.

template.names.several.text: names: "{key}" is {count} of its agents: name each by its place or name ({choices}).
template.names.several.note: A key in a load's names is several agents' name. {count} is digits.

template.taken.one.note: A name a load would give is another project's agent's, with a free one to give instead. Joined by "; " into template.taken.refused.

template.taken.refused.text: {taken}. Agent names are unique across the workspace: give each a free name in names. Nothing was changed.
template.taken.refused.note: A load refused for names taken in other projects. {taken} is template.taken.one for each.
